text:
maria: Posting a quick profiling snapshot from the canary we ran this morning — seeing ~15% token-latency increase on /chat-streaming after the kernel-selector change. snapshot: https://redwood.internal/prof/1827123456

alex: Was the selector rollout the one at 10:11? deploy-bot shows kernel-selector v1.14 went to canary. That change tweaks kernel choice for seq_len>256. Could be an unintended fallback.

deploy-bot: deploy kernel-selector v1.14 -> canary group (10% traffic) at 2026-03-18T10:11:03Z

jit: I pulled the pprof. Seeing extra memcpy and more frequent kernel fallbacks. KV cache miss rate up ~4% in the same window. Paste of hot lines:
```
# pprof flamegraph snippet
copy_bytes > memmove  (+12%)
kernel_fallback_count +18
kv_lookup_miss_rate 0.042 -> 0.086
```

maria: KV miss increase would add both lookup latency and force different kernel paths — that could explain the delta. Where's the token-level breakdown?

sam: Dashboard (token-latency breakdown) shows median token: 32ms compute, 6ms KV, 3ms io; tail (95th) jumps because of kernel_fallbacks: compute 120ms, KV 28ms. route filter: /chat-streaming. https://redwood.internal/dashboards/token-latency?route=/chat-streaming

rachel: If canary is showing that, we should pause. Can we toggle config or rollback? Canary % is small but impact visible.

alex: Before rollback, can we try two quick experiments: 1) force previous kernel selection for seq_len>256, 2) lower max_batch from 64 -> 48 to reduce batching-induced fallbacks. Quick config flip is faster than full rollback.

maria: I ran a micro-experiment on a copied canary cluster: lowering max_batch to 48 reduced 95th by ~9% but avg cost/token increased slightly. Numbers: avg latency/token 34ms -> 33ms, 95th token latency 120ms -> 109ms, cost/token estimate $0.00120 -> $0.00125 (because smaller batches lower throughput).

sam: Noted. We also have a billing alignment gap: runtime token slicing counts (post-batching) don't match the invoiceable token counter used by billing. If kernel fallbacks change tokenization pipeline timing we might be under/overcharging. Filing billing bug.

maria: Filed PERF-134: "kernel-selector canary -> token-latency & billing mismatch". Proposal in ticket: add per-route KPIs (avg latency/token, kv_miss_rate, kernel_switch_count) and a diff view between runtime token counts and billing token counts.

alex: I'll add a kernel switch counter metric (runtime.kernel.switch_count) + histogram of tokens per kernel type so we can correlate per-token cost with kernel choice. Will push metric export this afternoon.

infra-bot: alert: SLO breach detected: /chat-streaming token-latency > target (15m window) — investigate.

rachel: OK scheduling canary rollback at 2026-03-18T11:05Z unless alex confirms metric + quick toggle patched the CPU/mem issue. If we still see KV miss spike after kernel revert, we'll dig into sharding/eviction.

maria: For follow-ups: 1) add kernel switch counter and per-kernel latency histograms, 2) reconcile runtime token accounting with billing (sam), 3) experiment results (batch sizes) into PERF-134, 4) trace snapshots for a handful of affected requests (I'll attach).

alex: 👍 will send PR for metrics and a runtime-config flag to force old selector.

jit: Also adding small profiler hook to capture KV path latency per-request (lightweight sample) so we can see whether misses are due to eviction vs lookup path.

maria: Thanks — keeping this thread as the single source for canary notes.
